subject: Archaeology
title: Plaster Casts: Frozen in Time
description: A micro-lesson that makes Plaster Casts: Frozen in Time usable.

hook.text: In 1863, an archaeologist poured plaster into holes in the ash and created haunting casts of Pompeii's dead.

buildup.text: Giuseppe Fiorelli realized that bodies had decomposed, leaving hollow voids in the hardened volcanic debris.

discovery.text: The casts captured people in their final moments — a mother shielding a child, a dog straining at its chain.

twist.text: CT scans of the casts reveal bones, teeth, and expressions. One man appears to be screaming.

climax.text: Over 100 casts have been made. They turned an archaeological site into a memorial, making ancient death personal.

punchline.text: Volcanic ash erased their faces. Plaster gave them back.

quiz.question: How were the famous plaster casts of Pompeii created?
options: Artists sculpted them based on skeletal remains found at the site
Plaster was poured into body-shaped voids left in hardened ash
3D scanning reconstructed the victims from bone fragments

details.summary: In 1863, archaeologist Giuseppe Fiorelli developed the technique of pouring plaster into voids left by decomposed bodies in Pompeii's ash, creating haunting casts of victims in their final moments. These casts capture human emotion — terror, protection, embrace — with extraordinary immediacy.
details.whyItMatters: Fiorelli's technique transformed archaeology from treasure-hunting into human storytelling. The plaster casts make ancient death viscerally real, connecting modern viewers emotionally to people who lived two thousand years ago.
takeaways: Fiorelli poured plaster into body-shaped voids in volcanic ash
The technique captured victims' final postures and expressions
Casts revolutionized public engagement with archaeology

faq.question: How does the plaster casting technique work?
faq.answer: As bodies decomposed within the hardened ash, they left hollow voids preserving their exact shape. Fiorelli poured liquid plaster into these cavities through small holes. When the surrounding ash was removed, detailed casts revealed clothing folds, facial features, and body positions.

faq.question: Are modern casts still being made?
faq.answer: Yes, but now using transparent resin instead of plaster. CT scanning of both old and new casts has revealed bones, teeth, and artifacts inside without breaking them open, providing medical data about diet, disease, and age at death for Pompeii's final victims.
